title: Nehemiah Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Nehemiah chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Nehemiah Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Nehemiah Chapter 13.

questions.question: In Nehemiah 13, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Reading in the book of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: Reading in the book of Moses
questions.explanation: The reading in the book of Moses is the first event mentioned in Nehemiah 13:1.

questions.question: What was found written in the book of Moses?
options: The Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God
The Levites had fled to their fields
Balaam cursed the children of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God
questions.explanation: This is stated in Nehemiah 13:1, where it mentions the prohibition against the Ammonite and the Moabite.

questions.question: Why were the Ammonites and Moabites prohibited from the congregation of God?
options: They did not meet the children of Israel with bread and water
They refused to help during the Exodus
questions.correctAnswer: They did not meet the children of Israel with bread and water
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:2 states that the Ammonites and Moabites did not provide bread and water to the Israelites.

questions.question: What action did the Israelites take upon hearing the law?
options: They separated from Israel all the mixed multitude
questions.correctAnswer: They separated from Israel all the mixed multitude
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:3 indicates that upon hearing the law, they separated from all the mixed multitude.

questions.question: Who was allied to Tobiah?
questions.correctAnswer: Eliashib the priest
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:4 states that Eliashib the priest had the oversight of the chamber and was allied to Tobiah.

questions.question: What had Eliashib prepared for Tobiah?
questions.correctAnswer: A great chamber
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:5 mentions that Eliashib had prepared a great chamber for Tobiah.

questions.question: What was not given to the Levites?
questions.correctAnswer: Their portions
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:10 reveals that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them.

questions.question: What did Nehemiah do when he learned of Eliashib's actions?
options: He cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah
He sought counsel from the king
questions.correctAnswer: He cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:8 states that Nehemiah was grieved and cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah from the chamber.

questions.question: What did Nehemiah command to be done with the chambers?
questions.correctAnswer: They were to be cleansed
questions.explanation: According to Nehemiah 13:9, Nehemiah commanded that the chambers be cleansed.

questions.question: What did Nehemiah find out about the Levites and singers?
questions.correctAnswer: They fled to their fields
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:10 indicates that the Levites and singers fled to their fields because their portions were not provided.

questions.question: What did Nehemiah contend with the rulers about?
options: Why the house of God was forsaken
questions.correctAnswer: Why the house of God was forsaken
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:11 shows that Nehemiah contended with the rulers asking why the house of God was forsaken.

questions.question: The Ammonite and the Moabite are mentioned as forbidden in the congregation of God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:1 explicitly states that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God.

questions.question: Eliashib prepared a chamber for the Levites.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:5 specifies that Eliashib prepared a great chamber for Tobiah, not for the Levites.

questions.question: Nehemiah was present in Jerusalem during the time of Eliashib's actions.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:6 indicates that Nehemiah was not in Jerusalem at that time.

questions.question: The Levites had their portions provided to them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:10 states that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them.

medium.title: Nehemiah Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Nehemiah Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who were appointed as treasurers over the treasuries in Nehemiah 13?
options: Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah
Eliashib the priest, Tobiah, and Nehemiah
Hanan the son of Zaccur, and Mattaniah
Ezra the scribe, and the Levites
questions.correctAnswer: Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah
questions.explanation: This is found in Nehemiah 13:13, which lists the appointed treasurers.

questions.question: What does Nehemiah 13:14 promise will happen if someone keeps the house of God and its offices in good standing?
options: They will be remembered by God
They will prosper in all their ways
They will be protected from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They will be remembered by God
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:14 states, 'Remember me, O my God, concerning this...' indicating that good deeds will not be forgotten.

questions.question: What did Nehemiah witness some people doing on the Sabbath?
options: Treading wine presses and selling goods
questions.correctAnswer: Treading wine presses and selling goods
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:15 describes people treading wine presses and bringing in merchandise on the Sabbath, which he opposed.

questions.question: What does Nehemiah 13:18 warn will happen if the Sabbath is profaned?
options: They will be blessed by God
They will bring wrath upon Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They will bring wrath upon Israel
questions.explanation: In Nehemiah 13:18, Nehemiah argues that profaning the Sabbath brings more wrath upon Israel, referring to the past consequences.

questions.question: What action did Nehemiah take when he saw merchants outside Jerusalem on the Sabbath?
options: He commanded that the gates be closed
He welcomed them into the city
He reported them to the king
questions.correctAnswer: He commanded that the gates be closed
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:19 shows that he ordered the gates to be shut before the Sabbath to prevent burdens from being brought in.

questions.question: Why did Nehemiah contend with the nobles of Judah?
options: They were not giving their tithes
questions.correctAnswer: They were profaning the Sabbath
questions.explanation: In Nehemiah 13:17, Nehemiah contends with the nobles because they were profaning the Sabbath by their actions.

questions.question: What did Nehemiah do to ensure the Sabbath was sanctified?
options: He commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves
questions.correctAnswer: He commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:22 states that he commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves to sanctify the Sabbath day.

questions.question: What was Nehemiah's reaction to the actions of Eliashib regarding Tobiah?
questions.correctAnswer: He cast out Tobiah's belongings
questions.explanation: In Nehemiah 13:8, Nehemiah was grieved and cast forth all of Tobiah's household stuff out of the chamber.

questions.question: What did Nehemiah find was lacking when he returned to Jerusalem?
options: The Levites had not been given their portions
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites had not been given their portions
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:10 indicates that he perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them.

questions.question: What did Nehemiah do after finding that the house of God was forsaken?
options: He gathered the people to pray
He wrote a letter to the king
questions.correctAnswer: He contended with the rulers
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:11 shows that he contended with the rulers, asking why the house of God was forsaken.

questions.question: What was the consequence mentioned in Nehemiah 13:21 for merchants who continued to lodge outside Jerusalem on the Sabbath?
options: They would be punished by the king
They would not be allowed to enter again
questions.correctAnswer: They would not be allowed to enter again
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:21 records that he warned the merchants that if they continued their activities, he would take action against them.

questions.question: Nehemiah prayed to God to remember him for his actions regarding the house of God. This shows the importance of what?
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness in service
questions.explanation: Nehemiah's prayer in Nehemiah 13:14 reflects his desire for God to acknowledge his faithfulness in serving His house.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah found that the people were diligent in their observance of the Sabbath.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:15-18 illustrates that the people were profaning the Sabbath rather than observing it diligently.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah commanded that the Levites should cleanse themselves to sanctify the Sabbath day.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:22 indicates that he commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves for the purpose of sanctifying the Sabbath.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah allowed merchants to sell goods freely in Jerusalem on the Sabbath without any consequences.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:21 shows that he testified against the merchants and warned them not to continue their activities on the Sabbath.

hard.title: Nehemiah Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Nehemiah Chapter 13.

questions.question: According to Nehemiah 13:23, which groups did some Jews marry women from?
questions.correctAnswer: Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:23 specifically states that Jews had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.

questions.question: What linguistic issue did the children of these mixed marriages have according to Nehemiah 13:24?
options: They spoke half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language
They were fluent in both Jewish and foreign languages
questions.correctAnswer: They spoke half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:24 states that the children spoke half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language, but according to the language of each people.

questions.question: What action did Nehemiah take against those who married foreign wives as described in Nehemiah 13:25?
options: He contended with them, cursed them, smote some, plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God
He sent them away without confrontation
questions.correctAnswer: He contended with them, cursed them, smote some, plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:25 describes that Nehemiah contended with them, cursed them, smote certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God not to intermarry.

questions.question: Which king is mentioned in Nehemiah 13:26 as having sinned by marrying foreign women?
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:26 references Solomon king of Israel who sinned by marrying foreign women, causing him to sin despite being beloved of God.

questions.question: In Nehemiah 13:28, who was identified as being son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite?
options: One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest
questions.correctAnswer: One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:28 states that one of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite, leading to his expulsion.

questions.question: What did Nehemiah do after cleansing the priests and Levites from all strangers according to Nehemiah 13:30?
options: Appointed the wards of the priests and Levites, every one in his business
Appointed a new high priest from among the foreigners
questions.correctAnswer: Appointed the wards of the priests and Levites, every one in his business
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:30 explains that after cleansing them from strangers, Nehemiah appointed the wards of priests and Levites, each in his proper role.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'plucked off' (from Nehemiah 13:25) mean?
options: To tear out or pull off forcibly
questions.correctAnswer: To tear out or pull off forcibly
questions.explanation: In Nehemiah 13:25, 'plucked off' refers to forcibly tearing out hair as a sign of shame or punishment, consistent with the Hebrew root meaning.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in Nehemiah 13:23-27 where Solomon is mentioned as a warning?
questions.correctAnswer: Typology
questions.explanation: The reference to Solomon in Nehemiah 13:26 serves as typology, using a historical figure's experience as a moral example for present behavior.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of not marrying foreign wives as seen in Nehemiah 13:23-27?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 7:3-4
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 7:3-4 commands Israel not to intermarry with surrounding nations to avoid idolatry, directly connecting to Nehemiah's concern in 13:23-27.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the warning against intermarriage with unbelievers similarly to Nehemiah 13:23-27?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Corinthians 6:14-16
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 6:14-16 warns Christians against being unequally yoked with unbelievers, reflecting the Old Testament concern about intermarriage seen in Nehemiah 13:23-27.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Nehemiah 13:23 in the narrative?
options: Nehemiah commanding the Levites to cleanse themselves and keep the gates on the Sabbath
Nehemiah reading the book of Moses before the people
Nehemiah cleansing the chambers of Tobiah
Nehemiah closing the gates of Jerusalem at sundown on the Sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: Nehemiah commanding the Levites to cleanse themselves and keep the gates on the Sabbath
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:22 immediately precedes verse 23, where Nehemiah commands the Levites to cleanse themselves and keep the gates to sanctify the Sabbath.

questions.question: What historical-cultural context explains Nehemiah's strong reaction to intermarriage in Nehemiah 13:23-29?
options: Post-exilic concern for maintaining Jewish identity and covenant purity
Desire to expand political alliances with neighboring nations
questions.correctAnswer: Post-exilic concern for maintaining Jewish identity and covenant purity
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:23-29 reflects post-exilic efforts to maintain Jewish identity and purity of the covenant community after return from Babylonian exile.

questions.question: Which literary technique best describes Nehemiah's use of Solomon's example in 13:26 to warn against intermarriage?
questions.correctAnswer: Typological warning
questions.explanation: Nehemiah uses Solomon as a typological figure whose failure due to foreign wives serves as a warning, as stated in 13:26.

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah 13:29 calls upon God to remember those who defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the Levites.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:29 explicitly says, 'Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood, and the covenant of the priesthood, and of the Levites.'

questions.question: True or False: Nehemiah 13:31 records Nehemiah asking God to remember him for punishment because of his actions.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:31 says, 'Remember me, O my God, for good,' indicating a request for favor, not punishment.

theological.title: Nehemiah Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Nehemiah Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Nehemiah 13:1 teach about God's covenantal boundaries for His people?
options: God's covenant community is defined by obedience and separation from idolatrous peoples
God accepts all nations into His congregation without distinction
God's covenant is based solely on ethnic lineage regardless of behavior
God's covenant includes all who perform sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant community is defined by obedience and separation from idolatrous peoples
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:1 shows that the Ammonite and Moabite were excluded from the congregation because of covenant stipulations, teaching that God's covenant people are to separate from those who do not honor Him.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine providence and blessing underlies Nehemiah 13:2?
options: God can turn intended curses into blessings for His covenant people
Human effort alone determines blessing or curse
God is indifferent to curses pronounced by others
Blessings come only through ritual sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: God can turn intended curses into blessings for His covenant people
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:2 teaches that although Balaam was hired to curse Israel, God sovereignly turned the curse into a blessing, demonstrating divine providence over human schemes.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning sanctification and community purity is taught in Nehemiah 13:3?
options: The people of God must separate themselves from mixed or unclean elements to maintain holiness
All peoples are equally part of the congregation regardless of background
Sanctification is an individual, not communal, responsibility
Purity laws only apply to priests, not the entire community
questions.correctAnswer: The people of God must separate themselves from mixed or unclean elements to maintain holiness
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:3 shows that after hearing the law, the people separated from the mixed multitude, teaching that sanctification involves communal separation from impurity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Nehemiah 13:2 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:2 reveals God's sovereign control over curses intended by humans, as He reverses Balaam's curse into a blessing, demonstrating divine sovereignty.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Nehemiah 13:14 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:14 contains Nehemiah's prayer asking God to remember his good deeds and not wipe them out, appealing to God's mercy and faithfulness toward His servants.

questions.question: How does Nehemiah 13:19–21 connect to the broader biblical theme of Sabbath observance?
options: It reaffirms the Sabbath as a sign of covenant faithfulness and communal holiness
It introduces a new Sabbath law distinct from the Mosaic covenant
It suggests Sabbath observance is optional based on convenience
It relates Sabbath keeping only to temple rituals
questions.correctAnswer: It reaffirms the Sabbath as a sign of covenant faithfulness and communal holiness
questions.explanation: Verses 19–21 show Nehemiah enforcing Sabbath gate closures to prevent profaning the day, connecting to the biblical theme of Sabbath as a covenant sign of God's holiness and Israel's obedience.

questions.question: In what way does Nehemiah 13:23–25 prepare the narrative arc concerning intermarriage and faithfulness in Israel's history?
options: It highlights the ongoing threat of foreign influence leading Israel into sin, echoing Solomon's failure
It celebrates multicultural unity within Israel without restrictions
It ignores the issue of intermarriage as irrelevant to covenant faithfulness
It prescribes intermarriage as a means to political alliance
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the ongoing threat of foreign influence leading Israel into sin, echoing Solomon's failure
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:23-25 addresses intermarriage with foreign women causing language and covenantal breakdown, recalling Solomon's similar sin, thus preparing the narrative of covenant unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Nehemiah 13:10 and 13:11 teach about the relationship between community worship and leadership responsibility?
options: Leaders are responsible to ensure proper support and order for worship to prevent neglect
Worship is purely individual and not affected by communal leadership
Leaders should prioritize economic pursuits over worship responsibilities
The community is responsible alone without regard to leadership
questions.correctAnswer: Leaders are responsible to ensure proper support and order for worship to prevent neglect
questions.explanation: Verse 10 shows that Levites fled because they were not supported; verse 11 records Nehemiah contending with rulers to restore them, teaching leaders must uphold worship order and provision.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Nehemiah 13:19 and 13:22 teach about sanctification of the Sabbath and the role of the Levites?
options: Sanctification of the Sabbath involves both physical gatekeeping and spiritual cleansing by the Levites
The Levites have no role in Sabbath observance
Sabbath sanctification requires only ritual sacrifices but not community enforcement
The gates of Jerusalem remain open on the Sabbath for commerce
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification of the Sabbath involves both physical gatekeeping and spiritual cleansing by the Levites
questions.explanation: Verse 19 describes closing the gates to honor Sabbath; verse 22 commands Levites to cleanse themselves and keep gates, indicating both physical and spiritual roles in Sabbath sanctification.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Nehemiah 13:4 and 13:28 teach about the dangers of religious compromise and familial alliances with enemies?
options: Religious leaders must avoid alliances that compromise the holiness and covenant purity of the priesthood
Family ties with enemies strengthen the covenant community
Religious compromise is acceptable if politically expedient
Priests have freedom to associate with any without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Religious leaders must avoid alliances that compromise the holiness and covenant purity of the priesthood
questions.explanation: Verse 4 records Eliashib the priest's alliance with Tobiah; verse 28 shows Nehemiah expelling a priest's son-in-law allied with Sanballat, teaching that such compromises defile the priesthood.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Nehemiah 13:15-21 shows legalism and harsh enforcement of Sabbath laws. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches covenant faithfulness requires communal discipline to honor God's holiness on the Sabbath
It endorses Sabbath as an optional tradition without consequences
It promotes economic activity on the Sabbath as primary
It shows Nehemiah ignoring Sabbath concerns entirely
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches covenant faithfulness requires communal discipline to honor God's holiness on the Sabbath
questions.explanation: Verses 15-21 record Nehemiah's corrective actions against profaning the Sabbath, emphasizing covenant obedience and communal holiness rather than legalism.

questions.question: What doctrine does Nehemiah 13:29 teach about the relationship between covenant purity and the priesthood?
options: The priesthood's covenant and holiness can be defiled by unfaithfulness and must be remembered by God
The priesthood is immune to defilement regardless of behavior
Covenant purity is unrelated to priestly conduct
Priesthood status is only ceremonial and not covenantal
questions.correctAnswer: The priesthood's covenant and holiness can be defiled by unfaithfulness and must be remembered by God
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:29 prays that God remember those who defiled the priesthood and covenant, teaching the seriousness of covenant purity in priestly life.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Nehemiah 13:14 especially reflect through Nehemiah's prayer?
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:14 asks God to remember Nehemiah's good deeds, appealing to God's faithfulness in remembering His servants' obedience.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Nehemiah 13:12 and 13:13 teach about stewardship and communal support in God's covenant community?
options: Stewardship involves faithful collection and distribution of tithes to sustain those who serve in the house of God
Tithes belong only to the priests and not Levites
Material offerings are irrelevant to communal worship
Stewardship is a private matter with no public accountability
questions.correctAnswer: Stewardship involves faithful collection and distribution of tithes to sustain those who serve in the house of God
questions.explanation: Verse 12 records bringing tithes to treasuries; verse 13 appoints faithful treasurers to distribute, teaching responsible stewardship for community worship support.

questions.question: How does Nehemiah 13:31 connect to the biblical theology of offering and remembrance before God?
options: It emphasizes the importance of regular offerings and God's remembrance for good
It suggests offerings are unnecessary for God's favor
It depicts offerings as primarily for human status
It teaches forgetting past deeds before God
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the importance of regular offerings and God's remembrance for good
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 13:31 requests God remember him for good regarding offerings, underscoring biblical theology of offerings as acts of worship with divine remembrance.
